name: What is a second-story addition and how does it differ from a home extension?

mainEntity.name: What is a second-story addition and how does it differ from a home extension?

acceptedAnswer.text: A second-story addition involves building new living space directly on top of an existing single-story structure, expanding vertically without increasing the home's footprint. This is a common solution for adding bedrooms, bathrooms, or a master suite when lot size is limited. In contrast, a home extension typically expands the house horizontally, adding square footage to the side or rear of the property. While both increase living space, a second-story addition requires structural reinforcement and can be more complex due to vertical construction and integration with the existing roofline and foundation.
acceptedAnswer.description: A second-story addition builds new living space vertically on an existing single-story home, while an extension expands horizontally. Vertical additions require more structural work and do not increase the home's footprint.
